These include, but are not limited to the academic program, the curriculum, teacherand course feedback, academic clubs and activities, and undergraduate and postgraduate research. ● Coordinate between the Executives at the department level regarding issues that concern more than onedepartment. ● Coordinate the functioning of all the centralised facilities of academic nature, such as the Library, P. G. SenapathyComputer Centre, Placement Office, etc. along with the Research Affairs Secretary in a manner that addressesthe needs of the General Student Body. ● The Academic Affairs Secretary, along with the Research Affairs Secretary, shall be responsible for the smoothfunctioning of these facilities including, but not restricted to, the number, variety and quality of books andjournals available to the General Student Body. ● Be an ex-officio member of any committee, which may be set up by the Administration for matters related to theacademic affairs for taught programs. ● Be a member of the Sub-Committee for Discipline and Welfare of Students and regularly update the StudentLegislative Council and the General Student Body regarding the decisions taken by the Committee. ● Coordinate with the International and Alumni Relations Secretary on promoting research collaborations betweenIIT Madras and other premier Institutes/Universities in India and around the world. ● Be conversant with all the rules of academic research at the Institute. ● The following teams will be headed by the Academic Affairs Secretary: ➔ Placement & Internship Cell concerning the students of all the taught programs ➔ Career Development Cell 3 Placement & Internship Cell The Placement and Internship Cell shall facilitate industrial as well as academic opportunities via established processessuch as the Institute Placement Process & Institute Internship Process and other de-centralised processes. The cell shall be led by the Placement and Internship Governing Council, comprising of 5 Heads of the Placement &Internship Cell. They are: 1. Academic Affairs Secretary (AAS)2. Research Affairs Secretary (RAS)3. Placement Head (for all taught programs)4. Placement Head (for all research programs)5. Internship Head (for all taught programs) The team under the Placement and Internship Governing Council can be broadly divided into: 1. Verticals:a. These are the intra-department teams which are three-tieredb. The department teams will be separate for both the UG and PG programs, with representation for alldepartments in the UG and PG teams.c. The internship process will be jointly run by the same team for all the teams relevant to taughtprograms.2. Horizontals:a. These are the inter-department teams which are two-tieredb. These teams will handle all the things that aren’t under the purview of the department teams. Kindly refer to the Rulebook for the Placement & Internship Cell for more details. 4 Career Development Cell The primary duty of the Career Development Cell is to do all career development activities at a department level(through the Department Academic Mentorship program) and Institute level in coordination with CDC – R. In addition tothis, the CDC will look after the career-based clubs and the Student Guidance UG Team under the Placement &Internship Cell. Team Structure under the AAS CDC Heads The CDC Heads directly report to the AAS and are appointed through a written application and an interview process. Amaximum of 3 CDC Heads may be selected. The interview panel shall contain the AAS and outgoing CDC Heads. Advisor(CDC) may choose to have an additional interview process followed by the above-mentioned one. The CDC Heads are thede-facto Cores of the UG Student Guidance Team in the Placement & Internship Cell. Deputy Heads and Managers The CDC Heads shall select Deputy Heads and managers, in consultation with the AAS. The selection process is through awritten application and an interview. The interview panel shall contain the CDC Heads; the AAS may choose to join. TheCDC Deputy Heads and managers are the de-facto Deputy Heads and managers of the UG Student Guidance Team in thePlacement & Internship Cell. Duties and Responsibilities CDC is divided into 3 verticals. Each vertical would be assigned Deputy heads who would have the responsibility ofheading their respective verticals and managers who would be responsible for the operations of each vertical namely: 1. Placement and internship vertical: This vertical would have responsibilities of organising sessions to aid studentswith their placement and internship preparation, vendor outreach which can aid students in preparation, aidstudents to prepare in growing in their upcoming corporate careers and other activities which the appointedheads would see fit in counsel with the CDC heads.2. Future Prep vertical: This vertical would be responsible for helping students in their journey to find paths theycan take for their future by organising sessions and activities in the domain of higher studies, Competitive examsand Research, to handle niche career sessions, facilitate activities for students in tandem with the Universityrelations team and workshops and other activities which the appointed heads would see fit in counsel with theCDC heads.3. Mentorship vertical: The Mentorship team will handle the non-standard sessions and the Department AcademicMentorship program (DAMP) facilitating career development and academic activities at the department level.More detailed description of this vertical is mentioned on page 7. Other activities which the appointed headswould see fit in counsel with the CDC heads. 5 CDC would also have 2 responsibilities that the members of the above verticals would be made a part of in the semesterwhen the respective teams would have less workload as per the directions of the CDC heads. The teams would be: 1. Social media and Design team: This team would be responsible for designing content related to CDC, would beresponsible for the management of CDC’s social media accounts and other activities as suggested by CDC heads.2. Proprietary content team: This team would be responsible for generating content which CDC is responsible forlike Bluebooks, would be responsible for creating a short excerpt of all CDC events and other activities assuggested by CDC heads. Removal Procedure Removal from the team shall be for the following reason: Unsatisfactory Performance If a selected team member is found performing way below the expectations, he/she can be removed from the CDC teamfollowing due procedure. An initial warning shall be given, with a notice period of two weeks. If the performance doesnot improve in two weeks, the members higher in the hierarchy (if any), in consultation with AAS and Advisor (CDC), canchoose to remove the member from the team. A report on the same shall be submitted to the Advisor (CDC) and shall bemade available to SLC. 6 Department Academic Mentorship Program The Department Academic Mentorship Program (DAMP), managed by mentorship vertical - CDC, facilitates academicsand career mentorship at the department level. The primary target for the program is to guide second year and thirdyear dual degree students. A calendar for academic and career mentorship activities at a department level has to be created by the teamwhich will then be executed at the department level. Academic Advisor The Advisor will be educating students by providing guidance on topics including, but not limited to: ● The scope of the department and potential career opportunities ● The different specialisations offered by the program ● The kind of research opportunities the department offers ● Balancing academics and extracurricular activities ● Going about selecting courses and building a profile 7 The program will work complimentary to the existing mentorship programs and their activities would be kept in mindbefore starting new initiatives. An initial warning shall be given, with a notice period of two weeks. Affairs Secretaries shall be responsible for the satisfactory conduct of all literary/ arts/ social based cultural competitions and events in the institute. They shall strive to foster the arts, social and literary cultures in the Institute while creating avenues to nurture cultural talent. The Cultural Affairs Secretaries, with the guidance of the Cultural Advisor, will be responsible for the following matters: 1. Selection of the Institute Contingent; 2. Training and guidance for the cultural contingent; 3. Organising inter-hostel and inter-collegiate cultural events and competitions; 4. Maintaining an inventory of equipment used for arts and literary activities; 5. Involved in all matters of procurement of cultural equipment and maintenance of facilities; 6. Submission of all bills and vouchers to the Cultural Advisor; 7. Bringing information regarding the Cultural festivals of other institutes to the notice of the student body; 8. Organising the conduct of NCA activities; 9. Representing IIT Madras students at the Inter IIT Culturals Council. Resignation Procedure of the Cultural Affairs Secretaries Any member of the Executive Council who wishes to resign their Position of Responsibility may do so by writing a resignation letter to the Speaker and the Chairman, Board of Students, detailing the reasons behind the same along with the password to their official email id. A member of the Executive Council shall have resigned upon official communication of the same to the Student Legislative Council by the Speaker. Post-resignation Procedure In case a member of the Executive Council resigns with more than three months available for the scheduled General Elections, the Student Election Commission shall conduct an election for that particular Position of Responsibility immediately, with the student so elected continuing to hold office till the end of the academic year. In other cases, the Dean (Students) shall give additional charge of the vacated Position of Responsibility to a member of the Executive Council. Student Bodies under the Cultural Affairs Secretaries Saarang Saarang is the annual cultural festival of IIT Madras and is a Board of Students (BoS) associated organisation. A pioneering student fest of IIT Madras, it attracts over fifty thousand people from across the country every year and has been a host to performances from personalities within the country and from all over the world. It is an ISO affiliated completely student-run festival that is split into various departments for its effective functioning. The Cultural Affairs Secretaries are the overall students-in-charge of Saarang and have the authority to override the decisions made by any member of the Core Team. Organisational Structure The organisational structure of Saarang is hierarchical in nature, as illustrated below: Steering Committee The Steering committee for Saarang comprises the Director, all the Deans of the institute, full-time institute faculty members in-charge of various services of the institute, Chairman’s committee members, and the Core members. Chairman’s Committee The chairman’s committee comprises of the Dean (Students) (Chairman), Advisor (Cultural), full- time institute faculty, with at least one chairman committee member being in charge of Events and Prizes, Pro-shows, Hospitality, Safety & Security, Sponsorship and Public Relations, Publicity, Ticket Sales, Catering, Hygiene, Finance, Facilities, Transportation and Quality Management. Sub-Committee This is a committee comprising the core member of a service, a faculty member from the chairman’s committee who is in charge of that particular service, two full-time faculty members of the institute and a student member. Core Committee The Core committee for Saarang includes at least one committee member, each in charge of events, pro-shows, hospitality, safety & security, sponsorship and public relations, outreach, website operations, facilities & requirements, ticket sales, finance, media, ambience, design and quality management. The core member(s) in charge of a service is responsible for the design and development of that service. Managers, Strategists, Super-Coordinators & Coordinators They are appointed by the Saarang core committee with the approval of the Cultural Affairs Secretaries and include at least one person in charge of each event and facility at Saarang. The coordinators have the authority to take such decisions as they see fit with regard to the event or facility, but in case the core committee member in charge disagrees with the decision, the decision of the core committee member prevails. Volunteers They are appointed by the coordinators of the particular department. ** The structure and strength of the teams are subject to change every year with the discretion of the Cultural Affairs Secretaries or the respective cores of the team. The changes should be ratified by SLC and incorporated in the rulebook by the Standing Committee. The number of coordinators and super coordinators in each team is subject to change. The cores can add or remove members (with the approval of the Cultural Secretaries) if they deem it necessary for the improved functioning of the team. Departments under Saarang 1. Development and Mobile Operations The Development Operations team is an integral part of Saarang. It is responsible for creating and maintaining the Saarang website and Mobile app, and the Saarang Web 3.0 aspects. The team is also responsible for the creation and maintenance of the hospitality portal (used by the hospitality portal to keep track of the accommodations), the events portal (used by the events team to update the information of the various events), the sponsors portal (used by the sponsors ’team to update and manage the sponsors ’page) and the registrations app. Team Structure 3 cores (2WebOps + 1MobOps) 2 Strategists (DevOps + Web 3.0) 1 QMS Manager 3-4 Super-Coords (Variable) 5-6 Coords (Variable) 2. Events The events team of Saarang is what makes Saarang a true student-run fest. The cultural expertise and heritage that we have built over the years within the confines of the institute find its release at Saarang events. Having nearly 100 coordinators, it is also the biggest team at Saarang. The events are split into Non- Competitive, Competitive events and Saarang Nova. Non-Competitive Events: Informals and Meraki are dedicated to enveloping visitors in a blanket of fun and entertainment. Saarang Spotlight is our lecture-cum-demonstration series. Different workshops are organised under the banner of the cultural clubs. Informals and Meraki are dedicated to enveloping visitors in a blanket of fun and entertainment. Saarang Spotlight is our lecture-cum-demonstration series. Different workshops are organised by Saarang events and competitions team Competitive Events: Competitive events will be organised by different cultural clubs in the institute. Competitive events will be organised by Saarang events and competitions team Saarang Nova This vertical makes sure Saarang has something new to offer every year, keeping it unique and diverse. 3 cores 5 QMS Manager Super-Coords/Convenors (Variable) Coords (Variable) 2 cores 5 QMS Manager Super-Coords (Variable) Coords (Variable) 3. Facilities and Requirements The Facilities and Requirements team is the brain and the backbone behind LitSoc and Saarang. The F&R team has to manage various events under the purview of LitSoc, Saarang and Sangam. This involves a wide range of duties, including event management, material optimisation, cost optimisation etc. The coordinators have to use their management and people handling skills to interact with various people. This can vary from suppliers/ companies/ firms to procure materials and services to other coordinators to ensure a smooth and transparent material management process. The team also needs to develop shrewd skills to optimise the materials used. Coordinators would also be responsible for analysing data collected through various departments to optimise essential processes. Ultimately, the F&R team is responsible for arranging, optimising, and managing any facility inside or outside the institute to ensure that the institute's rich and unrivalled cultural scene runs in seamlessly and transparently. Team Structure: 3 cores 1 QMS Manager Super-Coords (Variable) Coords (Variable) 4. Finance The aim of the finance team is to ensure smooth, transparent and accounted flow of cash for the running of Saarang. The finance team ensures the optimal usage of money in Saarang. Finance does the monetary feasibility of initiatives proposed by other departments. The finance department constantly works on methods to decrease Saarang expenditures and improve its revenue. The finance team then works on areas where we can utilise the excess cash to take up the quality of Saarang. Team Structure: 2 cores 1 QMS Manager Super-Coords (Variable) Coords (Variable) 5. Media, Ambience & Design Media, ambience and Design is a service-oriented department that works on beautifying Saarang at each and every avenue possible. A professional and aesthetically appealing look is a necessity for the PR and the brand value of Saarang. Graphic design The team is responsible for designing posters for social media publicity, event notices, website, brochures and providing necessary support to the other sub-departments. Photography The team is responsible for capturing the moments of the fest (along with LitSoc). Videography This team is responsible for preparing promotional videos, teasers for Saarang, along with generating & editing the video footage of Saarang. Ambience This team is responsible for providing a festive feel to Saarang by decorating the festive area with various kinds of artworks. Team Structure: 4 cores (2 Design + 1 Ambience + 1 Media) 1 QMS Manager Super-Coords (Variable) Coords (Variable) 6. It is one of the very few teams which brings in revenues of this scale. With a significant chunk of the sales now being shifted online, they will be working on a targeted approach and focusing more on the marketing part to optimise our sales. The team is also responsible for taking Saarang to the rest of the world. From ideation to execution, these coordinators will handle publicity events in Chennai and other cities (Milan). The publicity team works on shaping Saarang’s image throughout the year and ensuring that we are able to reach out to the relevant audience. Coordinators will also be available to work dedicatedly on the club and LitSoc publicity at any point in time. Team Structure: 2 cores 1 QMS Manager Super-Coords (Variable) Coords (Variable) 7. It is one of the very few teams which brings in revenues of this scale. With a major chunk of the sales now being shifted online, they will be working on a targeted approach and focus more on the marketing part in order to optimise our sales. Team Structure: 2 cores 1 QMS Manager Super-Coords (Variable) Coords (Variable) 8. Professional Shows The professional shows department is responsible for the organisation and execution of the 5 OAT Night Shows and the World Fest. Coordinators are involved in a wide array of tasks such as ideation, negotiation of artiste fees, artiste selection, production, and creating and executing a publicity plan. With the largest budget and the added fact that the professional shows act as the public face of Saarang to our larger audience, the Professional Shows teams get a major say in defining the look and feel of Saarang as a whole. Team Structure: 2 cores 1 QMS Manager Coords (Variable) Deputy Coords (Variable) 9. Quality Management Systems The Quality Management Systems (QMS) Department of Saarang is responsible for the ISO Certification of Saarang annually. QMS strives to improve the organisational standards of Saarang by making Saarang process-oriented, defining the processes involved in each department and ensuring that the quality is maintained at each step. QMS is also responsible for the maintenance of the Saarang Quality Standards Manual. QMS should essentially act as a bridge between all the departments by ensuring smooth interdepartmental interactions, and regular follow up of various activities. Aspects of QMS will also play a significant role in the Cultural clubs of the institute and Lit-Soc as well. Sustainability Vertical: To enhance and improve the sustainability of the fest, a sustainability vertical will be introduced under QMS, where a few managers will be allotted to work on the aspects of sustainability for the fest. Analytics Vertical: To help understand and analyse the previous year sales, footfall and set parameters for improvement, an Analytics vertical will be introduced as a part of the QMS team. Team Structure: 2 cores 1 Sustainability Strategist 1 Analytics Strategist 15 Managers 10. Crowd management and ensuring no chaos inside the OAT, and avoiding unpleasant incidents in the audience through proper screening at entry points are part of their team responsibilities. Team Structure: 2 cores 1 QMS Managers Super-Coords (Variable) Coords (Variable) 11. It primarily consists of two teams, the Sponsorship & the Creatives team. It’s the responsibility of the Sponsorship team to reach out to the maximum possible number of sponsors, come up with innovative deliverables and create a long-term, mutually beneficial relationship with them. They need to exhibit utmost professionalism at all times. Ultimately, the objective is for the sponsors of Saarang to leave with the best branding experience for their products. The Creatives teams must understand the different aspects of their multi-faceted job and take up each with responsibility and conviction. They should innovate while managing and creating creative- content for all the existing social media handles. They should also look for new avenues to enhance the Saarang brand amongst our target audience. Team Structure: 3 cores 1 QMS Managers Coords (Variable) Creative and Media Coords (Variable) Sangam Sangam is the Committee of all the Cultural Clubs in the institute. Events Constitution 2022-23 Website: https://sangam.iitm.ac.in Sangam will be headed by 3 Sangam Cores who will also be the official Contingent Leads representing IIT Madras in the Inter IIT Cultural Meet . Preparing a structured timeline at the beginning of each semester and ensuring adherence to planned activities. Appointing club heads and overseeing the selection process of deputy club heads and contingent members. Planning the contingent selection process at the start of the odd semester, immediately following Club Weekender. Cultural Affairs Secretary, Executive Committee According to the constitution: “ Each Executive Council Member shall form a committee to assist him/her. The core members of the committee shall be nominated by the respective executives in consultation with the Faculty Advisors and ratified by the SLC. The coordinators shall be selected by the respective core members” Cultural Affairs Secretary Executive Committee shall compose of the following structure post consultation with the faculty advisor: 5 cores 10 Coordinators Cultural Affairs Alumni Committee The Cultural Affairs Alumni Committee is to serve as a close group of advisors for the incoming set of cultural secretaries; bridging the gap between alumni and the current team for the betterment of culturals in the institute. The committee would include former cultural secretaries, led by a chairperson elected by committee members if the position is deemed necessary. Each year, outgoing cultural secretaries would automatically become new committee members, while additional members would be invited by existing committee members. This structure aims to ensure continuity and effective knowledge transfer, providing a platform for experienced individuals to offer guidance and support to incoming cultural secretaries and core team members. The formation of this committee and incorporation of new members would be intimidated to the Cultural Advisor, DoSt and steering committee members, if necessary for better connect and communication between the alumni and the administration. The responsibilities of the Alumni Committee encompass assisting current cultural secretaries and core team members in decision- making in Sangam, Saarang, Inter IIT, and other cultural activities. They are tasked with providing valuable insights and support to ensure a smooth transition and successful execution of events and activities. Additionally, the committee oversees the implementation of long-term projects aimed at benefiting the cultural landscape of the institute, while also offering initiatives, visions, and ideas for the incoming team to execute. Moreover, members are expected to be willing to provide support in terms of contacts, sponsors, finances, and other resources as needed. Other roles and responsibilities, if any of the committee would be decided upon by the members and the new cultural secretaries. Statement of Expenditure The Cultural Secretaries and Sangam Cores shall present a financial statement detailing the expenditure of the approved budget at least once a semester to the Student Legislative Council in addition to a report about their financial statement to the corresponding Standing Committee. Failure to do the same may lead to the initiation of contempt proceedings against the secretary/body and bring them/it to the Student Legislative Council for further action. Selections The cores of the departments are appointed by the Cultural Affairs Secretaries and the Cultural Advisor. The Strategists, Managers, Coordinators, Heads, Super coordinators and Deputy Coordinators are selected by the respective cores of the department. Eligibility Criteria The positions of volunteer, deputy coordinator, coordinator, super coordinator, manager and strategist, and head positions are open for all members of the general student body. All applicants to the core positions must satisfy the following conditions: ● In the case of B. Tech., DD, M. Tech., MA, MBA, M.Sc., M.S., and PhD., students, the applicant’s CGPA must equal or exceed 6.50 at the date of applying; ● M.S. and PhD research scholars should have completed, satisfactorily, all the required courses for which they have registered and should have received the scholarship amount uninterruptedly; ● The applicant should not have been implicated in an academic disciplinary committee action; ● The applicant must not have been found guilty of any gross misconduct by the Hostel Disciplinary Committee, Complaint Committee Against Sexual Harassment or any similar competent authority; ● The applicant should not have "U" or "W" grades in their grade card; ● It is mandatory to have at least one year of relevant experience to apply for the position of Core. In case an applicant who does not satisfy the above conditions has to be selected, prior approval has to be obtained from the Dean (Students) and the Cultural Advisor, and the selection has to be ratified by the Student Legislative Council (SLC). Procedure for Selections All selections are based on a written application which will be followed by an interview round. The selection of the core committee is conducted by the incoming Cultural Affairs Secretaries and Cultural Advisors in consultation with the outgoing core committee. - The application questionnaire for the aspiring cores is made by the outgoing core committee, in consultation with the Cultural Affairs Secretaries. - It is the prerogative of the Cultural Secretaries to decide the selection criteria for the new core team. However, the criteria of selection have to be communicated with and approved by the Cultural Advisor. - Core Team members of all departments are selected by the Cultural Secretaries based upon Application & Interview process & with the consultancy of previous year Saarang Core Team and the Cultural Advisor. - Selections for all non-core positions are to be carried out by the newly selected core committee members in consultation with the Cultural Affairs Secretaries. - It is the responsibility of all team members to ensure that proper knowledge transfer occurs between the ongoing year’s teams and the incoming team. - It is recommended that the outgoing core team arrange knowledge transfer sessions towards the end of their tenures and document the minutes of their debriefing meeting so as to aid the process of knowledge transfer. Removal Procedure Removal from the team shall be for three broad reasons: 1. Unsatisfactory performance 2. Disciplinary Action 3. Financial Misappropriation Unsatisfactory Performance If a selected team member is found performing below the expectations, they can be removed from the team following due procedure. An initial warning shall be given, with a notice period of two weeks. If the performance does not improve in two weeks, the members higher in the hierarchy (if any), in consultation with the Cultural Affairs Secretaries and the Cultural Advisor can choose to remove the member from the team. A report on the same shall be submitted to the Cultural Advisor and shall be made available to SLC. Disciplinary Action In case any complaint is received against any selected member of the team accusing them of disciplinary violations, this shall be taken seriously and can serve as grounds for termination from the team. A committee shall be constituted by the Cultural Affairs Secretaries within 48 hours of receipt of the complaint. The committee shall investigate the complaint thoroughly, the report of which will be made available to the SLC and submitted to the Cultural Advisor along with a recommendation to remove the said person from the team if found guilty. Further, being found guilty and facing disciplinary action in any of the disciplinary committees or statutory bodies such as the Committee for Complaints Against Sexual Harassment (CCASH) can be deemed legitimate grounds for removal of a person from a team, upon the discretion of the Cultural Affairs Secretaries. Any action taken in this regard must be communicated to the Cultural Advisor, and also documented internally within the team. Financial Misappropriation When a complaint is lodged regarding financial misappropriation against any core/ position holder, it should be referred to the Financial Accountability Committee (FAC). The FAC submits the report (preferably two weeks after the complaint is lodged) to the Cultural Affairs Secretaries and Cultural Advisor. The decision of the Cultural Affairs Secretaries and the Cultural Advisor is final in this regard.

files.c043c99d0d: Rule Book - Institute Sports Secretary IIT Madras Seventh Version – 10th June 2023 Proposed by: Abhishek Katre Institute Sports Secretary 2023-24 Section 1 - Roles and Responsibilities: The Institute Sports Secretary shall: 1. Look after all issues regarding the sports activities of the students. 2. Be responsible, with the assistance of the Physical Training Instructors, for the following matters: a. Selection of Institute Teams b. Coaching c. Organizing inter-hostel and inter-collegiate matches 3. Help the Institute Sports Advisor and Co-Advisor in coordination, planning and execution of all sporting activities. 4. Be involved in all matters of procurement of sports equipment and maintenance of facilities. 5. Be responsible for the signing and submission of all bills and vouchers to the Sports Advisor. 6. Be responsible for bringing information regarding the Sports tournaments of other Institutes to the notice of the student body. Section 2 - Team Structure: ● Sports Organizing Committee ● Institute Team Captains ● Representatives ● Hostel Sports Council 2.1 Sports Organizing Committee (SOC) The Sports Organizing Committee is a student body under the Institute Sports Secretary that shall be responsible for organizing all the sporting activities in the Institute. The Committee shall strive to promote sportsmanship and transparency in the sporting culture of the Institute. The Sports Organizing Committee shall also organize inter-college tournaments, including, but not limited to Jimmy George, Sports Fest, and GF&KR; and propose the budget for all sporting activities that come under the Gymkhana 2.1.1 RESPONSIBILITIES OF THE SPORTS ORGANIZING COMMITTEE HEAD(S) ● The Head(s) shall act as the Point of Contact between different departments of the SOC, the sporting clubs, and the Gymkhana. ● The Head(s) shall facilitate the smooth- functioning of the various sporting activities that are organized in the institute. ● The Head(s) shall oversee the functioning of different departments of the SOC, from planning to execution. 2.1.2 RESPONSIBILITIES OF THE FINANCE, ADMINISTRATION, & SALES TEAM: ● Obtaining lists of requirements from captains, conveners, representatives, and the SOC team. ● Budgeting for the sporting aspects of the Gymkhana and acting as a bridge between SOC activities, ISS’s initiatives, representatives’ initiatives, institute captains, and the administration. ● Maintaining an inventory of the equipment falling under the Institute Gymkhana. ● Keeping track of transactions, purchases, and the general finances related to sports. ● Handling the sale of general and club merchandise during Agrata and making sure the process is hassle-free and efficient ● Assisting other teams in case of an online tenure. 2.1.3 RESPONSIBILITIES OF THE SPONSORSHIP AND PUBLICITY TEAM: ● Contacting Alumni and various companies, to garner funds for sporting equipment/ requirements. ● Raising sponsorship for Agrata, Inter-IIT teams, SOC Clubs, ISS Initiatives, and any applicable SOC events. ● Looking after the publicity and branding for the Inter-IIT contingent. ● Working to improve the sporting atmosphere at the institute. ● Running the PR Campaign for the sporting sphere throughout the year. ● Ideating and executing publicity related to any sporting event on campus. 2.1.4 RESPONSIBILITIES OF FACILITIES, HOSPITALITY & OUTREACH TEAM: ● Handling all the logistical and material requirements involved in organizing and promoting all sports events in the institute including but not limited to booking venues, arranging PA systems and projectors, and printing posters and banners. ● Taking care of accommodation for institute-organized sporting events including but not limited to GF&KR, Jimmy George, and Sports fest. ● Ensuring outreach to other institutes and colleges to maximize the publicity and impact of events conducted by SOC. ● Maintaining & Expanding relations with other colleges with regard to events organised by the Institute. 2.1.5 RESPONSIBILITIES OF THE DESIGN AND AMBIENCE TEAM: ● Ideating and creating posters and banners for all the important sporting events happening in the Institute. ● Designing T-shirts for SOC, jerseys for the Institute sports teams, brochures, and the annual sporting magazine. ● Handling the ambiance for events including but not limited to the theme launch of Agrata, NSO orientation, Agrata, and the PR Campaign launch. 2.1.6 RESPONSIBILITIES OF THE MEDIA TEAM: ● Providing media coverage for all the important sporting events happening in the institute. ● Controlling the YouTube channel of IITM Sports with content involving but not limited to tutorials, the know your team series, teasers, after-movies, promo videos, and interviews of eminent sports persons. 2.1.7 RESPONSIBILITIES OF THE CONTENT TEAM: ● Ideation and curation of yearbooks, magazines, record books, articles, blogs, and podcasts. 2.1.8 RESPONSIBILITIES OF THE WEBOPS TEAM: ● Handling all the work associated with the IITM Sports Website, including all updates and maintenance of the website and any other additions to it. ● Maintenance and constant updation of the Grievance Portal. ● Updating the results of all Sporting Activities in the Institute on the website. ● Making the website for Agrata and handling all related to digitalization. 2.1.9 RESPONSIBILITIES OF THE EVENTS TEAM: ● Planning and conducting informal events for Agrata. ● Handling all collaborations with other teams in the institute for events conducted by SOC. ● Planning of regular events to engage the GSB with the sporting sphere. ● Coordinating with all the club conveners and ensuring the smooth functioning of all the institute sporting clubs. ■ The Events Team Core(s) stand as the organizers of sporting club-related events. ■ The Events Team Core(s) will act as a point of contact between the conveners, SOC heads, ISS, and Gymkhana. 2.1.10 ROLES & RESPONSIBILITIES OF THE WOMEN’S REPRESENTATIVE: ● The Women’s Representative should necessarily be a student from the female student community of the institute. ● She shall work to improve the sporting culture among the female students in the institute. ● She will be responsible for conducting Women’s Schroeter in a hassle-free manner. ● She shall voice the concerns and the requests of the women sports enthusiasts to the Institute Sports Secretary. ● She shall aid all the women’s teams in performing their best at the Inter-IIT Sports Meet and other competitions representing IIT Madras. 2.1.11 ROLES & RESPONSIBILITIES OF THE PG REPRESENTATIVE: ● The PG Representative should necessarily be a student from the PG student community of the institute. ● He/she is responsible for organizing events that will improve the PG participation in sports by being sensitive to their needs/academic schedules. ● He/she shall voice the concerns and requests of the PG sports enthusiasts to the Institute Sports Secretary. ● He/she shall be responsible for ideating and executing beginner camps, PG leagues, and any other event that would benefit PGs in coordination with the SOC teams and the club conveners. 2.1.12 SELECTION PROCEDURE: ● The Selection process for the Head, Reps and Cores includes a well-drafted written application and an interview done by the ISS, ex-cores & heads, ex-reps as applicable to each position. ● The Selection process for the coordinators includes a well-drafted written application and an interview done by the core(s) of the respective department. ● All applications will be evaluated internally using a points + voting system involving all interviewers. Results of this evaluation will be presented to the SLC for ratification of all core team positions. 2.1.13 REMOVAL PROCEDURE: ● Unsatisfactory Performance: ● If a core is found performing way below expectations, he/she can be removed from the SOC following due procedure. An initial warning shall be given, with a notice period of two weeks. If the performance does not improve in two weeks, the Head(s) of the SOC, in consultation with ISS and Advisor (Sports), can choose to remove a core from the team. A report on the same shall be submitted to Advisor (Sports) and shall be made available to the SLC. ● If a coordinator is found performing way below expectations, the concerned core shall issue a warning, with the Head(s) of the SOC in the loop. If the performance does not improve in two weeks, the coordinator shall be removed from the team, in consultation with the Head(s) of the SOC, ISS, and Advisor (Sports). A report on the same shall be prepared by the concerned core and presented to the ISS. ● Financial Misappropriation: ● When a complaint is lodged regarding financial misappropriation against any core/coordinator in the Sports Action Committee, it should be referred to the Financial Accountability Committee (FAC). The FAC submits the report (preferably two weeks after the complaint is lodged) to the Institute Sports Secretary and Advisor (Sports). The decision of the ISS and Advisor (Sports) is final in this regard. 2.2 Institute Team Captains The Institute Team Captains lead their respective teams at all inter-collegiate and other levels of sporting tournaments, including but not limited to the Inter IIT Sports Meet, Agrata and other competitions conducted by IIT Madras. 2.2.1 SELECTION PROCEDURE ● The team captains will be selected by the team members, coach, and PTIs (Physical Training Instructors) in consultation with the Institute Sports Secretary. 2.2.2 ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF THE INSTITUTE TEAM CAPTAINS Their responsibilities include: ● Conducting Institute practice sessions. ● Representing their sport in the Inter-Hostel Sports Board. ● Planning and managing activities related to the Institute team. ● Voicing the concerns and the requests of the Institute Team Members of their respective sport to the Institute Sports Secretary. Captains shall be selected for the following sports: ● Athletics (MEN & WOMEN) ● Badminton (MEN & WOMEN) ● Basketball (MEN & WOMEN) ● Chess ● Cricket (MEN) ● Football (MEN) ● Hockey (MEN ) ● Squash (MEN & WOMEN) ● Swimming (MEN & WOMEN ) ● Table Tennis (MEN & WOMEN ) ● Lawn Tennis (MEN & WOMEN ) ● Volleyball (MEN & WOMEN) ● Water polo (MEN) ● Weightlifting (MEN) In the absence of a captain, the vice-captain of the team, appointed by the coach and respective PTI along with the ISS, shall take over the responsibilities. 2.3 Institute Team Vice-Captains ● The team vice-captains will be selected by the team members, coach, and PTIs (Physical Training Instructors) in consultation with the Institute Sports Secretary 2.3.1 ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF THE INSTITUTE TEAM VICE CAPTAINS ● Shall be a part of the insti sports team. (If applicable)Shall plan and manage the activities of their respective club. ● Shall maintain detailed documentation of all the events that are organized by the respective club ● Conduction of Club weekenders, freshie orientations, NSO day, Freshie IDL, Schroeter, IDL, Dean’s trophy, NSO, etc. ● Organizing practice matches for the institute teams. ● Conduction of all the initiatives of the ISS falling under the purview of the sporting clubs. ● Conduction of club centric culture events. ● Maintenance of club handles on social media pages.. 2.3.2 Captains shall be selected for the following sports: ● Athletics (MEN & WOMEN) ● Badminton (MEN & WOMEN) ● Basketball (MEN & WOMEN) ● Chess ● Cricket (MEN) ● Football (MEN) ● Hockey (MEN ) ● Squash (MEN & WOMEN) ● Swimming (MEN & WOMEN ) ● Table Tennis (MEN & WOMEN ) ● Lawn Tennis (MEN & WOMEN ) ● Volleyball (MEN & WOMEN) ● Water polo (MEN) ● Weightlifting (MEN) 2.3.3 REMOVAL PROCEDURE ● If a vice-captain is found performing way below the expectations, he/she can be removed from his/her position following due procedure. An initial warning shall be given, with a notice period of two weeks. If the performance does not improve in two weeks, the Institute Sports Secretary in consultation with the captains can choose to remove that convener from the team. A report on the same shall be submitted to the Advisor (Sports). 2.4 Sporting Clubs Sporting clubs are student bodies under the events cores, captains and vice captains and monitored by the Institute Sports Secretary, who shall be responsible for all the activities related to that particular sport. The club shall function in coordination with the SOC and the Institute Team Captains and vice captains. Institute team club will be under the vice-captain and overseen by the captain. The Club shall strive to promote their sport in the sporting sphere of the institute. The club structure is as follows: ● Club Convener (Selected Position) ● Club Executives (Selected Position) ● Club Members (Not a selected position: Anyone interested can join the club) The list of Sporting Clubs whose sports are a part of the Inter IIT Sports Meet is as follows: (Note: the inter iit team clubs will be under vice captains and overseen by the captains no conveners will be appointed for them) ● Aquatics Club ● Athletics Club ● Badminton Club ● Basketball Club ● Chess Club ● Cricket Club ● Football Club ● Hockey Club ● Squash Cub ● Table Tennis Club ● Tennis Club ● Volleyball Club ● Weightlifting Club The list of other Sporting Clubs is as follows: ● Bridge Club ● Cycling Club ● Frisbee Club ● Adventure Club ● Gymnesia club (new club) 2.4.1 SELECTION PROCEDURE FOR CONVENERS ● Conveners will be selected by the Events Core(s) & Institute Sports Secretary based on the application and interview process. ● These are subject to change under the discretion of the Institute Sports Secretary and the Sports Advisor. 2.4.2 ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF THE CLUB CONVENER ● Shall be a part of the sports sub-committee. (If applicable) ● Shall plan and manage the activities of their respective club. ● Shall maintain detailed documentation of all the events that are organized by the respective club. ● Conduction of Club weekenders, freshie orientations, Freshie IDL, IDL, Dean’s trophy, NSO, etc. ● Conduction of all the initiatives of the ISS falling under the purview of the sporting clubs. ● Conduction of club centric culture events. ● Maintenance of club handles on social media pages. ● Coordinating with club executives. 2.4.3 REMOVAL PROCEDURE ● If a convener is found performing way below expectations, he/she can be removed from his/her position following due procedure. An initial warning shall be given, with a notice period of two weeks. If the performance does not improve in two weeks, the Institute Sports Secretary in consultation with the SOC Head(s) can choose to remove that convener from the team. A report on the same shall be submitted to the Advisor (Sports). Section 3 - Resignation Procedure: 3.1 PROCEDURE: ● The Sports Secretary can resign his/her Position of Responsibility by writing a resignation letter to the Speaker and the Chairman, Board of Students, detailing the reasons behind the same along with the password to their official email id. The Sports Secretary shall have resigned upon official communication of the same to the Student Legislative Council by the Speaker. 3.2 POST-RESIGNATION PROCEDURE: ● In case the Sports Secretary resigns with more than three months available for the scheduled General Elections, the Student Election Commission shall conduct an election for that particular Position of Responsibility immediately, with the student so elected continuing to hold office till the end of the academic year. In other cases, Dean (studentsts) shall give additional charge of the vacated Position of Responsibility to a member of the Executive Council. Section 4 - Finance: 4.1 BUDGET: ● The Sports Secretary shall consolidate the proposals presented to him/her by the student bodies that report to him and shall work along with the Standing Committee (Sports) to prepare the final budget. The Student Legislative Council may approve the budget demanded by the Sports Secretary or can make modifications to it as it deems necessary. For the budget to be approved, two-thirds of those present and voting must approve. 4.2 STATEMENT OF EXPENDITURE: ● The Sports Secretary and his/her team shall present a financial statement detailing the expenditure of the approved budget at least once a semester to the Student Legislative Council in addition to a report about their financial statement to the Standing Committee (Sports) once in two months. Failure to do the same may lead to the initiation of contempt proceedings against the Sports Secretary and bring him/her to the Student Legislative Council for further action.

It is organized annually among all the IITs by rotation/mutual consent at minimum two or more IITs. I. AIMS AND OBJECTIVES 1. The primary objective of Inter IIT Sports Meet shall be to organize sports competitions in selected Olympics recognized events. This meet aims encourage sportsmanship, to promote and create a better harmony, understanding and friendly interaction among the students of the IITs, as well as to foster a close association among them. 2. To make the students aware of the importance of sports and games in the modern era. 3. To help students perform skillfully and effectively not only in sports, games and exercises but also in all situations. 4. To raise the standard of sports in IITs and to work for the development of character and values through sports among the students of the IITs. 5. To discuss matters related to the organization of sports and other such activities that support the aims and objectives of the Inter IIT Sports Meet, as mentioned above. 6. The Sports Meet shall be conducted in accordance with the provisions mentioned in succeeding paragraphs, which may be revised from time to time . II. INTER IIT SPORTS BOARD • The Inter IIT Sports Board shall be constituted for the purpose of effective supervision of the Inter IIT Sports Meet. The headquarters of the Sports Board will be located at all the hosting IITs. The Sports Board is constituted with the following members: 1. The Directors of the hosting IITs will be the Chairperson of the Inter IIT Sports Board. 2. The Deans, Students’ Affairs of the hosting IITs will be the Chairpersons of the Inter IIT Sports Meet. 3. Chairpersons/Faculty advisors of each hosting IITs will be the Conveners of the Inter IIT Sports Meet. 4. One Physical Education staff of each hosting IITs will be the Organizing Secretaries of the Inter IIT Sports Meet. 5. Chairpersons/Faculty advisors of participating IITs at each hosting IIT will be the members of the Inter IIT Sports Meet. 6. One Physical Education staff of participating IITs at each hosting IIT will be the member of the Inter IIT Sports Meet. 7. One st udent General Secretary, Sports/student nominee of participating IITs at each hosting IITs will be the member of the Inter IIT Sports Meet. • Chairperson of the Sports Board shall preside over all Sports Board’s meetings in the respective IITs. In his/her absence, the Chairperson of the Inter IIT Sports Meet or Convener of Inter IIT Sports Board shall occupy the chair and conduct the proceedings of the meetings. The minutes of all the meetings shall be recorded and circulated to the members of all IITs immediately after each meeting. • The quorum for conducting of the Sports Board meeting shall be a minimum of half or more of the total members of the Sports Board. All proceedings shall be decided by a majority of votes. In case of a tie, the Chairperson or his/her nominee shall make the final decision on the matter. • The Sports Board of the Inter IIT Sports Meet may co-opt any individual in an advisory capacity, to be a member on ad hoc basis, without any voting right. • The Sports Board shall meet at the at one of the hosting IITs, as soon as possible, after the academic session begins for the year in which the Inter IIT Sports Meet will be conducted. The Board shall have two more mandatory meetings at the host IITs, one on the day preceding the inauguration of the Sports Meet and the other before the closing ceremony of the Sports Meet. Additional meetings shall be organized as desired by the Board. • In pursuance of the responsibilities vested in the Inter IIT Sports Meet Board, it shall have the following specific powers in connection with the conduct of the Sports Meet. a) To co-ordinate the Sports Meet, finalize the dates and to draws fixtures/schedule of the Meet. b) Addition or deletion of any sports/events. c) To amend, modify, formulate or delete the rules of Inter IIT Sports Meet with majority of votes among the present board members. d) To discuss matters related to the organization of sports and to promote other such activities that may be conducive to the aims and objectives of the Inter IIT Sports Meet. e) All the c ompetition shall be conducted as per the federation rules for each games and sports implemented by Indian Federations, or any modification approved by the board, till the date of the board meeting in August of the respective year. f) Over and above these powers, the Inter IIT Sports Board shall be the final authority to decide on any matter(s) arising during the Sports Meet and its decisions shall be binding to all the IITs. III. ELIGIBILITY All Bonafide students of all IITs, who will be getting degree/diploma from the concerned IITs, shall be eligible to participate in Inter IIT Sports Meet. A consolidated list of the contingent members, attested as Bonafide students by the Dean of Students/Registrar of concerned IITs, should be submitted to the convener of the meet before its commencement. IV. CONTINGENT STRENGTH I. The maximum strength allowed for any individual IIT is 185. II. Out of the 185 students for the regular sports events, the maximum numbers of girls allowed are 50 (excluding chess). This number will be reduced to 47, if the girls’ contingent fails to participate in all of the events. III. The maximum number of boys allowed is 129 (excluding chess). The entries shall be sent to organizing secretaries by the participating IITs well in advance so that when the Sports Board meets during its first meeting in August, the Sports Board is able to arrange the entire program of the Sports Meet. Seeding will be awarded to the first four/two position holders of the respective game in the previous meet. Only two seeding will be given, if ten or less teams are participating in the respective game. Four teams will be given seeding, if more than ten teams are participating in the respective game. The remaining teams shall be considered by drawing lots for each game during the first meeting of sports board. iii. The schedule of the matches will be in accordance with the model fixture provided in the attached annexure. iv. If one team withdraws its entry and if, it was in the pool of 4 teams, no redraw of fixtures will be done. Similarly, if one team withdraws in a game having only two pools, no redraw of fixtures will be done. v. In all other cases of withdrawal of one or more teams, redrawing will be done and the previous fixture will be considered as null and void. vi. The team withdraw from fixture will be banned for next year in the respective game. vii. Organizing committee has the right to alter the schedule of the program under unusual circumstances. VII. The average points of the march past at all opening ceremonies of the meet will be co nsidered for d eciding overall c hampionship trophy. ii. The aquatic sports will be organized at one of the hosting IITs. iii. Separate Championships will be awarded to Men and Women, based on their respective points tally and points awarded for March past & chess will not be considered in it. iv. Amendments taking place after the first Sports Board meeting shall be followed only from the subsequent Inter IIT Sports Meet. IX. TROPHIES AND CERTIFICATES i. Winner, 01st Runner-up & 02nd Runner-up trophies of all the events, as well as Men, Women and Overall Championship trophies are rolling trophies in the Inter IIT Sports Meet. ii. A list of all the trophies, which are available for the award shall be maintained by the Sports Board and printed (at the end of the handbook) from time to time in the handbook of competition rules for the Inter IIT Sports Meet. iii. An IIT which wins the Overall Championship for three consecutive times will be presented with a memento by the host of the subsequent Inter IIT Sports Meet. iv. In team games, the trophies and medals shall be awarded only to winners, runners up and the second runners up of each game. v. Certificates of merit shall be awarded to the winners, runners up, second runners up and the fourth place of each game, signed by the Chairperson, Convener and the Organizing Secretary of the Inter IIT Sports Board. vi. Player excellence award (Best athlete/player) certificates and trophy will be awarded for all the sports as per resolution of the Inter IIT sports board meeting held in 2016. vii. A team/competitor shall be permitted a grace of 15 minutes from the schedule timings of the event and then a walk-over shall be awarded unless genuine reason(s), beyond control, are presented and accepted by the Board. ii. For all games and sports, the decision of the referees and the umpires will be final and binding to all participants. iii. No protest shall be entertained. Therefore, any team leaving the field of play as a mark of protest and conceding a walk-over shall be deemed to have lost the fixture and will be eliminated from rest of the event. Only the remaining teams will be considered as participating in that event. iv. Protest against the decision of an umpire/referee on a point of rule and any other protest in connection with the concerned match/event shall be given in writing addressed to the Jury of appeal along with a protest fee of Rs.500. v. The written protest must reach the Organizing Secretary of the host institute within an hour of the conclusion of the concerned game duly signed by the competent authority of that particular IIT. vi. If tie still persists, t he team winning m aximum number of silvers will be awarded the championship and so on. vi. The progression after every successful attempt for the same weightlifter must be minimum of 1 Kg. vii. Certificate shall be awarded to the first four places in all weightlifting categories. viii. The competitors should wear only ‘position slips’ and no oil or grease should be applied on the body at any stage. BEST LIFTER Sinclair coefficients formula: The Sinclair coefficients, derived statistically, are adjusted each Olympic year and are based on the Total World Records in the various bodyweight categories as of the previous several years. ACTUAL TOTAL x SINCLAIR COEFFICIENT = SINCLAIR TOTAL The Sinclair Total is calculated by taking an athlete’s total (combined max snatch and clean & jerk) and multiplying that number by the Sinclair Coefficient. Example: Who is the strongest? If 50kg man totals 178kg, the 100kg man totals 303kg and the 130kg man totaling 323kg? The math looks like: 50kg male has a Sinclair coefficient of 1.713308. 178kg (total) x 1.713308 = 304.969 (Sinclair Total) The 100kg male’s coefficient is 1.112602. 303kg (total) x 1.112602 = 337.118 The 130kg’s coefficient is 1.030222. 323kg (total) x 1.030222 = 332.762 The strongest man by this definition is the 100kg man. Sinclair scores more fairly c omparing lif ters of different body w eights. The score is obtained by multiplying the lifter's Snatch and Clean & Jerk total by a coefficient which is based on body weight. The total lifts of the gold medal winners in every weight class at each Olympic Games are used to determine the formula that will be used for calculating Sinclair coefficients. Thus, Sinclair coefficients and scores are only valid for the four-year period commencing on 01 January of the year immediately following an Olympic Games. XXIX. If any student found guilty, he/she will be debarred from the competition and will be stripped off his/her medal(s). The coach of respective event will also be punished. files.9018fb16b0: Indian Institute of Technology Madras Chennai, India-600036 Rulebook for Student Legislative Council 1 Table of Contents I. SLC Meetings II. Teams under the Speaker 1. Secretariat Team 2. Public Policy Club III. Parliament Trip 2 I. SLC MEETINGS RULES AND PROCEDURE 1) Convening Meetings A. SLC meetings shall be convened by the SLC Speaker, the dates of the meetings shall be informed to the Legislators at least a week in advance. B. In case the Legislators are not informed a week in advance, the so-convened SLC meeting will have to approve the meeting through a simple majority, failing which the SLC meeting shall automatically be considered Null and Void. C. An SLC meeting can also be convened by a 1/3rd of SLC Legislators by a written application to the SLC Speaker. Section (1.a) applies here too. 2) Agenda Points A. The Speaker shall call for Agenda for an SLC meeting 7 days before the SLC meeting , the agenda point should be proposed by Legislators only. However, the suggestions from GSB shall be taken into consideration by the SLC Legislators. B. The agenda for the SLC meeting shall be finalised by the SLC, 4 days before the meeting. The Agenda shall be shared in the SLC Google Group. The Agenda shall be considered valid unless a simple majority of SLC members vote to change/modify the agenda. C. The Agenda shall be publicised at least 24 hours before the SLC meeting. D. Any point not on the Agenda shall be raised only if the SLC agrees to discuss the same through a simple majority. E. Minutes of an SLC meeting shall be circulated within seven days of the Meeting among GSB. 3 3) Attendance, Non-Transferable Vote and Disqualification A. Seeing that the dates of the SLC meeting are to be conveyed a week in advance, it is reasonable to expect all the SLC Legislators to attend all the meetings. In case a Legislator knows that he/she will be unable to attend the SLC meeting, he/she must inform the same to SLC Speaker within 3 days of the Speaker announcing the date. B. The Secretariat head shall take attendance at the start of every meeting. C. In General, the vote of a SLC Legislator is non-transferable, i.e. in case of absence, a proxy shall not be allowed to take part in the SLC meeting on a Legislator’s behalf. However, in case of special circumstances/ unforeseeable events (the validity of which is to be decided at the Speaker’s discretion), the Legislator may nominate a member on his/her behalf to an SLC meeting. Such nominations shall not exceed 2 meetings in a given year. D. Any Legislator who remains absent for more than 50% of the meetings (the integer value to be determined by the ceiling function) shall automatically stand disqualified as an SLC Legislator. The same shall be conveyed by the Speaker to the Legislator and the GSB within a week. E. In case the concerned electorate wants to nominate another Legislator to SLC instead of the disqualified Legislator, it can do so if at least 25% of the electorate writes a signed letter to the Speaker. The Speaker shall take the necessary measures to facilitate this process. The Speaker shall confirm and inform the GSB about the nomination after having ensured the authenticity of the letter - a process that must be completed within a week of receiving the letter. 4 4) Speaking Time and Censure Motion A. Only those Legislators who are recognized by the Speaker shall talk in the SLC. Each Legislator can’t talk for more than 3 minutes at a stretch without the Speaker’s permission. Members of the GSB can speak only with the Speaker’s approval. B. The Speaker shall have the power to censure a Legislator for unparliamentary behaviour on the SLC floor. The Speaker shall provide justification for the same within a week. Three Censures in an academic year shall automatically lead to disqualification. C. The SLC has the power to Censure an Executive Council Member or the SLC Speaker for unconstitutional behaviour. This Censure Motion will have to be passed by 2/3 rd of the Legislators. When the censure motion is against the SLC Speaker, the Deputy Speaker shall preside over the SLC meeting. The Deputy Speaker shall be selected from the Legislators by simple majority. 5) Referendum A. Initiation: A referendum shall be initiated by the Speaker only if more than half the total strength of SLC, more than half the EC or more than 500 members of the GSB ask for it through a signed memorandum addressed to the Speaker. B. Procedure: The Speaker shall conduct a referendum within 48 hours of receipt of the memorandum. C. A referendum shall be considered valid if and only if more than one-third of the total GSB cast their vote and a motion shall be considered as passed only if a simple majority of these vote in favour of the motion. 5 II. TEAMS UNDER THE SPEAKER 1. SECRETARIAT TEAM A. Purpose The Student Legislative Council's (SLC) Secretariat serves as the SLC's administrative backbone and support structure, ensuring that it runs smoothly. It is essential for streamlining the legislative procedure and helping the Speaker do their duties. B. Responsibilities of the Secretariat team The Student Legislative Council Secretariat, under the leadership and guidance of the Speaker, is in charge of looking after the publicity and facilities requirements of the Student Legislative Council and its committees. In addition, the Secretariat shall carry out those duties and responsibilities that are assigned to it by the Speaker insofar as it relates to fulfilling the Speaker’s constitutional obligations. a. Administrative Assistance: The Secretariat offers the Speaker crucial administrative assistance, facilitating the efficient conduct of the SLC meetings. It helps with scheduling, keeping track of paperwork, and managing official correspondence. The Secretariat's management of administrative and logistical duties frees up the Speaker to concentrate on their leadership duties and strategic decision-making. b. Procedural Assistance: During council sessions, the Secretariat aids the Speaker in following legislative rules. It assists in ensuring that meetings are conducted in a fair and orderly manner by advising participants on procedure, keeping minutes, and controlling voting procedures. The Secretariat contributes to maintaining a nicely organised and effective legislative environment by offering expertise in legislative procedures. c. Maintaining records and documentation: The Secretariat is in charge of keeping complete records of council proceedings. It creates and maintains legislative papers like minutes and resolutions. By preserving the institutional memory of the SLC and facilitating access to historical 6 information for reference and accountability needs, the Secretariat maintains conversations, decisions, and actions taken by the council. d. Managing Effective Communication: On behalf of the SLC, the Secretariat promotes internal and external communication, ensuring that information is effectively communicated to council members, Executive Council, the general student body. e. Student Engagement & Outreach: The Secretariat serves as a point of contact for students, responding to their questions, requests, and issues. It offers information, advice, and referrals to pertinent council members or committees as part of its constituent services. To encourage student engagement and raise knowledge of the SLC's programmes, the Secretariat also plays a role in publicising council activities, events, and accomplishments. f. Assisting Standing Committees: i) Mid-Term and End-Term Reports: The Secretariat supports standing committees in preparing mid-term and end-term reports of the Executive Council (EC) for town hall meetings. It assists committees in gathering relevant data, analysing EC activities, and drafting comprehensive reports that highlight achievements, challenges, and future plans. The Secretariat ensures that these reports are well-structured, accurate, and provide a clear overview of the Executive Council's performance. ii) Manifesto Reviews: The Secretariat maintains documents related to the manifesto reviews of EC members, legislators, and hostel council members. It assists standing committees in compiling and organising the necessary information for evaluating the progress made towards fulfilling manifesto promises. The Secretariat ensures that the manifesto review documents are securely stored, easily accessible, and regularly updated to track the implementation of key initiatives. C. Composition The Secretariat shall consist of: 1. 1 Secretariat Head 2. 2 Strategists (Operations & Outreach and Documentation & Reporting) 3. Coordinators (maximum of 7) 7 D. Selection The student-head of the secretariat shall be appointed by the Speaker subject to ratification by the Student Legislative Council. The Secretariat heads shall in turn appoint the strategist and coordinators in consultation with the Speaker. E. Term of Office Each member shall have a term of office of one year. F. Eligibility The eligibility of the members of the Public Policy Club shall be as follows: A. No Academic or Hostel disciplinary actions B. A minimum CGPA of 6.5 C. On-campus resident D. No U/W grade E. No C-Cash proceedings G. Removal Procedure If a Head/Strategist/Coordinator is found performing way below expectations, the Head shall issue a warning, if the said complaint is on the Head, the Speaker shall issue a warning. If the performance does not improve within a span of two weeks, the said individual shall be removed from the team, in consultation with the Speaker. The report on the same shall be prepared by the concerned punitive authority. H. Resignation of members of the Secretariat Members of the Student Legislative Council Secretariat may tender their resignation by writing to the Speaker. A member shall have resigned from the Secretariat once all financial transactions carried out by him/her have been settled and the same is notified to the Student Legislative Council by the Speaker. 8 2. PUBLIC POLICY CLUB A. Purpose The Public Policy Club falls under the SLC Speaker's jurisdiction. The club aims to establish an environment conducive to facilitating intellectually stimulating parleys on contemporary policy. The Club is directly accountable to the SLC speaker. With an unwavering commitment to innovative policy solutions, the club serves as a catalyst for positive change, actively influencing policy discourse and driving socio-economic development at institute as well as national level. The Public Policy Club at IIT Madras envisions a transformative platform that critically interweaves academia and policy formulation, benefiting the General Student Body (GSB). By fostering a culture of critical thinking and evidence-based decision-making, the club empowers members to become effective policymakers and advocates. Through engaging dialogues and interdisciplinary collaboration, it cultivates a deep understanding of pressing socio-political issues. Organising seminars, workshops, and conferences, the club bridges the gap between theory and practice, facilitating meaningful discussions with policymakers, practitioners, and experts. B. Responsibilities of the Public Policy Club a. Policy Education and Training: Workshops and Skill-Building Sessions: To improve members' comprehension of policy-making processes, research methodologies, critical analysis, and effective communication, the club holds workshops and training sessions. b. Policy Debates and Discussions: The group hosts debates and discussions on current policy problems, giving members a forum to voice their thoughts, have a productive conversation, and develop their critical thinking abilities. c. Analysing Policy Proposals: The club evaluates policy proposals and their potential impact on the student community, providing thoughtful analysis and recommendations to the SLC. d. The Public Policy Club actively tries to collaborate with other student groups and organisations that have a similar focus on public policy or related subjects. e. Reporting and Accountability: The Public Policy Club shall provide regular reports on its activities and achievements to the SLC. The team is 9 responsible for documenting and summarising club activities, participation, and outcomes. This information shall be presented at designated SLC meetings or as requested by the Speaker or relevant standing committees. C. Composition The team shall consist of: 1. Heads (Maximum of 2) 2. Vice-Heads (Maximum of 3) 3. Coordinators (Maximum of 8) D. Selection The heads of the Public Policy Club shall be appointed by the Speaker subject to ratification by the Student Legislative Council. The club heads shall in turn appoint vice heads and coordinators in consultation with the Speaker. E. Term of Office Each member shall have a term of office of one year. F. Eligibility The eligibility of the members of the Public Policy Club shall be as follows: A. No Academic or Hostel disciplinary actions B. A minimum CGPA of 6.5 C. On-campus resident D. No U/W grade E. No C-Cash proceedings G. Removal Procedure If a Head/Vice-Head/coordinator is found performing way below expectations, the Head shall issue a warning, if the said complaint is on the Head, the Speaker shall issue a warning. If the performance does not improve within a span of two weeks, the said individual shall be removed from the team, in consultation with the Speaker. The report on the same shall be prepared by the concerned punitive authority. 10 H. Resignation of members of the Public Policy Club Members of the Public Policy Club may tender their resignation by writing to the Speaker. A member shall have resigned from the club once all financial transactions carried out by him/her have been settled and the same is notified to the Student Legislative Council by the Speaker. III. PARLIAMENT TRIP A student delegation trip to the Parliament of India would be conducted under the purview of the Speaker, the Student Legislative Council Secretariat Team and the Public Policy Club. The trip would be held during the winter session of the Parliament which coincides with the student’s winter break. The trip would comprise a visit to the Parliament during session, meetings with Ministers and Members of Parliament, sessions and/or workshops with think tanks and NGOs and a social awareness visit. The aim of the trip would be to educate the General Student Body on topics of governance, policy and politics and encourage the delegation to foster the same level of discussion in the student governance ecosystem of the institute. Selection of Delegates: The delegation would comprise members of the Executive Council, Student Legislative Council, SLC Secretariat Team, Public Policy Club, FAC, T5E, SECC, and selected delegates from the General Student Body. The selection of the delegates would be done by the SLC Secretariat and the Public Policy Club through a rigorous screening process comprising an application and an interview. 11

A report on the same shall be submitted to the Chairman of the respective committee and shall be made available to SLC. A committee shall be constituted by the Hostel Affairs Secretary within 48 hours of receipt of the complaint. The committee shall investigate the complaint thoroughly, the report of which will be made available to the SLC and submitted to the Chairman of the respective committee along with a recommendation to remove the said person from the team and prior work will not be credited if found guilty. Further, being found guilty and facing disciplinary action in any of the disciplinary committees or statutory bodies such as the Committee for Complaints Against Sexual Harassment (CCASH)can be deemed legitimate grounds for removal of a person from a team, upon the discretion of the Hostel Affairs Secretary. Any action taken in this regard must be communicated to the Chairman of the respective Committee and also documented internally within the team.
