About IAR Sphere 1.1 Vision The International & Alumni Relations sphere serves as the prominent representative of IIT Madras within and beyond the institution. Its primary objective is to enhance alumni relations, cultivate a favourable local and global perception of IIT Madras, foster valuable corporate opportunities, and actively promote and facilitate international exchanges. The IAR sphere encompasses esteemed entities such as the Office of Alumni & Corporate Relations, the Office of Global Engagement, the IIT Madras Alumni Association, the Heritage Centre and the IAR Student Council. Through cohesive collaboration, these entities diligently cooperate with other student and administrative organizations, strategically aligning efforts to achieve the visionary goals envisioned by IITM. 1.2 Structure 3 2. Team’s Structure & Responsibilities 2.1 Alumni & Corporate Relations Council 2.1.1 Alumni Relations Cell Vision ● To connect the IIT Madras alumni community to its students and facilitate their interactions with the administration, alum association, and office. ● Create channels for knowledge and information transfer from the alums to the student community and bring mentorship opportunities. Roles of the team in the IAR Student Council ● Facilitate flagship events like Reunions and LLS in collaboration with the office. ● Engage alums in social and corporate-related events by institute teams and even from other universities/colleges for the IIT Madras community. Structure 4 Roles & Responsibilities Heads ● To represent the student community and IAR council at the ACR office and & IITMAA along with the IAR Secretary. ● To lead and execute the projects involving the alum community proposed by the IAR secretary and the team. ● Mentor and guide the managers and strategists through the project cycles and processes. Strategists ● To lay out structure and execution strategies for the projects, in collaboration with managers and with the consultation of heads & IAR Secretary. ● To lead the managers and the volunteers through the project process and execution. ● To facilitate team cohesion and a feeling of ownership among the managers and the volunteers towards the projects and the council. Managers ● Collaborate with fellow managers and strategists to devise elaborate project plans and communicate with the stakeholders and collaborators to lead the projects to completion. ● To lead and manage the volunteers to achieve project goals and represent the IIT Madras student community to respective stakeholders & collaborators. ● To foster and maintain relations of the IAR council with the student community and ensure equal and fair opportunities. Selection Criteria ● Heads: CGPA >= 6.5; no U, W, or I grade at the time of application; No disciplinary action (DISCO, CCASH) taken against the applicant; 3rd years and above. ● Strategists: 3rd-year students and above. ● Manager: 2nd-year students and above. 5 2.1.2 Corporate Relations Cell Vision ● The IAR Student Council Affinity Program aims to bridge the gap between institution and industry for better opportunities for students. The program will achieve this by: ● Onboarding sponsors for events under IARSC. ● Enhancing public relations by conducting various events like Net-Vest, Industry Day ● Providing students with opportunities for building their careers through associations with corporate. ● Facilitating student life by bringing affinity deals, and social initiatives like Saarthi fund. Role in the IAR Student Council ● Raising sponsorship for events under IARSC. ● Bagging affinity deals for institute students and alumni. ● Organizing events like Net-Vest and Industry Day. ● Coordinating with the student council to smoothly execute all the events. ● Setting up the foundation for Saarthi fund, an emergency medical relief fund for the students of IIT Madras and their immediate family members. Structure 6 Roles and Responsibilities Heads ● Smoothly lay the foundation of new initiatives & events including NetVest & Sawera. ● Lead the team to raise the academic year’s sponsorship for events by the IAR Student Council and by offices. ● Ensure the team brings in associations for the students and alumni as a part of the Affinity Program. ● Lead the team to promote and upscale the Affinity Program. ● Lead the team in ideating for the campaign and other events. Strategists ● Train the managers and scrutinize the work to assure quality checks on the working of the team overall. ● Raise sponsorship amount and handle associations with larger companies. ● Ideate and execute the CSR Fundraising campaign. ● Ensure that the deals by their managers are executed properly and guide them in the same. ● Ideate on events and publicity and work on the execution. Managers ● Handle kind and PR deals and associations for the Affinity Program ● Ideate and execute the CSR campaign and events. ● Work on publicity and up-scaling of the Affinity Program. Selection Criteria The selection criteria for all positions are as follows: ● Presentation skills ● Communication skills ● Confidence ● Enthusiasm ● Initiatives and ideas \ 7 2.2 Branding Council 2.2.1 Chennai36 Vision Chennai 36, or C36 as it is fondly called, is the writing arm of IAR Council's Branding Cell, the official student and alumni blog within the institute. We aim to connect the various stakeholders groups like current students, alumni, etc through the medium of writing. The main goal of Chennai36 is to highlight the accomplishments, experiences, and stories of IIT Madras students and alumni, while engaging with the faculty and fostering dialogues for showcasing the research and innovation in the institute. The blog focuses on a variety of topics, such as research endeavours, entrepreneurial ventures, extracurricular activities, and interviews with eminent alumni. It provides an avenue for recognising the successes and efforts of the IIT Madras community while also educating and motivating its audience. Role of the team in the IAR Student Council C36 conducts interviews and writes articles about various topics ranging from internships to general fundaes. We also conduct the DAA interviews and are involved in producing the content for the yearbook. This year, C36, apart from its regular activities, will also be managing/producing content for Campus Times, a campus reprise of the older Campastimes. Some of our regular interactions and collaborations include: ● DAA Interviews: IITMAA, Alumni Relations Office Yearbook: ARC, Design Team ● Campus Times: Heritage Club, Design Team ● Blog/Website: WebOps, Design Team Structure 8 Roles and responsibilities Head ● Responsible for managing the team ● Determining the direction of the blog and the nature of articles ● Facilitating collaborations with other IITM student bodies and relevant offices ● Allocating tasks to editors and ensuring accountability ● Ideating on better reach among the students Editors ● Responsible for managing the correspondents ● Ensuring timely submissions and editing the articles ● Ideation for social media, blog design, content, etc ● Leading different initiatives for the blog ● Ensuring team bonding with the correspondents ● Compiling Campus Times Correspondents ● Responsible for content generation ● Following the deadlines for articles/interviews ● Conducting interviews ● Generating content for Campus Times ● Producing creative content for the yearbook Selection Criteria Important: In the event that there are less than the required number of applications to fill positions in the Editorial Team then a dynamic form of recruitment will be executed on a rolling basis. As and when suitable candidates are identified they will be inducted in the team following an application process. Selection Criteria & Process for Heads: ● Experience and Expertise: Candidates with a proven track record of editorial leadership, exceptional writing skills, and knowledge of the content covered by Chennai36 may be preferred. 9 ● Leadership Abilities: Leadership qualities such as strong decision-making skills, the ability to manage a team, delegate tasks, and provide guidance are important criteria for this role. ● Editorial Vision: The Heads should have a clear vision for the magazine's content, tone, and objectives. They should be able to articulate their vision and demonstrate how they would contribute to the growth and development of Chennai36. ● Teamwork and Collaboration: As the head of the team, the Heads need to work closely with other editors, correspondents, and stakeholders. The ability to foster a collaborative and inclusive work environment, effectively communicate ideas, and delegate responsibilities is crucial. ● Adaptability and Time Management: Publishing written work often involves strict deadlines and managing multiple tasks simultaneously. The Heads should be able to handle pressure, manage time effectively, and adapt to changing circumstances. ● Selection Process: The selection process for the Head position will involve a combination of application evaluation and interviews with the outgoing Heads and the IAR Secretary where candidates will get the opportunity to outline their editorial vision and strategies for Chennai36. Selection Criteria & Process for Editors & Correspondents ● Application: Interested individuals will need to submit an application expressing their interest in joining the Chennai36 team after the applications have been released on smail. ● Evaluation of Application: The Heads will be reviewing the applications to assess the suitability of candidates. They may look for qualities such as strong writing skills, creativity, enthusiasm, and a genuine interest in contributing to the platform. ● Shortlisting: Based on the evaluation, the editorial team shortlists candidates who meet the initial criteria and have shown potential to contribute effectively. Shortlisted Editor candidates will be invited for an interview whereas the correspondents may or may not have an interview depending on the decision of the Heads. The interview will help to assess the candidates' communication skills, passion for writing, ability to work in a team, and their understanding of the Chennai36’s objectives and content. ● Writing Samples: Candidates may be requested to provide additional writing samples or a mock interview with a guest to evaluate their writing capabilities along with their skills in conducting an interview. ● Selection: After considering the applications, interviews, and writing samples, the Heads will make the final decision regarding the selection of editors and correspondents for Chennai36. The selected individuals are notified and offered positions within the team. 10 2.2.2 Institute Branding Cell Vision ● To attract the top minds (students and professionals) of the country and the world to IIT Madras and build a long-term, positive and productive relationship with various facets of the community we are engaged with. ● To make IBC as the face of IIT Madras branding. ● Boosting the institute’s brand image in the global community, including, but not limited to aspiring students, our international partners/universities, our esteemed alumni, academia, and the corporate sphere. ● Disseminating knowledge about the overall life and exposure that IITM provides to its students. Role of the team in IARSC ● IBC helps in fulfilling IARSC vision of establishing the global brand of the institute by conducting events and increasing social media presence of IARSC. Each event reaches out to the various stakeholders of IARSC. These events include, a day @ iitm, Sawera, parents day, institute mascot launch and branding conclave. IBC also handles IITM gift shop. The goal is to attract top talent from foreign universities and promote the exchange of students, graduate students, and interns. Role of the team in the IAR Student Council ● The team plays a vital role in promoting collaborative research projects between IIT Madras and international institutions. ● By facilitating the exchange of knowledge, research findings, and expertise, the team enables the growth of academic collaborations and the advancement of scientific and technological knowledge. ● The team strives to make international opportunities more accessible to the student body at IIT Madras. ● They provide information and support to students, enabling them to take full advantage of the institute's partnerships, Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs), and collaborations with international institutions. ● This helps students explore study-abroad programs, internships, research opportunities, and other avenues that contribute to their academic and professional growth. 21 Structure Roles and Responsibilities Head ● Structuring Research Process: The Heads are responsible for organizing and structuring the research process to identify potential tie-ups and collaborations with international universities and industry partners. ● Delegating Tasks to Managers: The Heads delegate executable tasks to the team's managers based on their skills and expertise. These events contribute to improving the global perception and visibility of the institute. ● Collaboration with Other Student Teams: The Team Head explores the possibility of collaborations with other student teams within the IAR Student Council and other institute teams. files.a28de65de8: IIT MADRAS Research Affairs Secretary Rule Book (Version 7.0) Proposed on: 11/06/2023 1 Table of Contents ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: 2 RESEARCH AFFAIRS SECRETARY – TEAMS: 3 1. Research Affairs Secretary (RAS) Executive Team: 4 3. Career Development Cell – Research (CDC-R) Team: 8 4. Research Scholars Day (RSD) Team: 10 5. Research Connect (R-Connect) Team: 14 6. Problem Solving Cell-Research Team: 16 7. Research-Clubs (R-Clubs) Team: 19 Research Affairs Council (RAC) 21 RESIGNATION PROCEDURE 21 Resignation of the Research Affairs Secretary: 21 Post-resignation Procedure: 21 STATEMENT OF EXPENDITURE 21 ANNEXURES 22 History of Edits 22 2. Placement & Internship Cell 4 2 Roles and Responsibilities: The Research Affairs Secretary shall: A. Represent the views of the students from research programs on matters related to academic research to the Board of Academic Research and the Senate. These include, but are not limited to the research programme, the curriculum, teacher, guide and course feedback, and postgraduate research; B. Coordinate between the Executives at the depar tment level regarding issues which concern more than one department; C. Coordinate the functioning of all the centralized facilities of academic nature, such as the Library, the P. G. Senapathy Computer Centre, the Placement Office etc. along with the Academ ic Affairs Secretary in a manner that addresses the needs of the General Student Body. The Research Affairs Secretary, along with the Academic Affairs Secretary, shall be responsible for the smooth functioning of these facilities including, but not restricted to, the number, variety and quality of books and journals available to the General Student Body; D. Be an ex -officio member of any committee which may be set up by the Administration for matters related to the affairs of academic research of the students; E. Be a member of the Academic Disciplinary Committee and regularly update the Student Legislative Council and the General Student Body regarding the decisions taken by the Committee; F. Be a member of the Ethics Committee and regularly update the Student Legislative Council and the General Student Body regarding the decisions taken by the Committee for issues regarding unethical publishing/plagiarism etc. G. Coordinate with the International and Alumni Relations Secretary on promoting research collaborations between IIT Madras and other premier Institutes/Universities in India and around the world; H. Be conversant with all the rules of academic research of the Institute. 3 Research Affairs Secretary – Teams: Below is an overview of the structure of teams which come under the aegis of the Research Affairs Secretary. 4 1. Research Affairs Secretary (RAS) Executive Team: This team shall comprise of minimum 1 and a maximum of 5 members selected from the electorate to help the RAS to implement new initiatives and ideas and in general assist him/her with the execution of the tasks under his/her purview. The outgoing or an ex -RAS shall be a de -facto member of this team and shall play an advisory role. Executives Coordinators: The Coordinators shall be selected through a written application and interview process, with the panel containing the RAS and the Executives Team. The coordinators shall be allocated based on the team’s requirements removal is as other teams. 2. Placement & Internship Cell: The Placement and Internship Cell shall facilitate industrial as well as academic opportunities via established processes such as the Institute Placement Process & Institute Internship Process and other de- centralised processes. RAS during the 2023-2024 academic year proposed a new placement division that deals with the academics related opportunities is planned to be created under the existing placement cell. This idea arrived from the recent placement statistics indicating the scholars are equally motivated to take the academic positions like pdf positions, Faculty positions,, Teaching positions , Foreign exchange programs, and Research associate at prestigious institutes in India. The academic placement head works under the RAS and need to report to the RAS. The motive of this division is to provide the academic opportunities to the scholars. The head is responsible to identify the vacancies related to the faculty positions at various institutes and make them available to the scholars either by on -campus or off -campus means. This initiative helps scholars land in academic roles at premier institutes. 5 6 Team Structure Placement & Internship Governing Council The cell shall be led by the Placement and Internship Governing Council, comprising of 5 Heads of the Placement & Internship Cell. They are: 1. Academic Affairs Secretary (AAS) 2. Research Affairs Secretary (RAS) 3. Placement Head (B. Tech, Dual Degree, M.A.) 4. Two Placement Head (M. Tech, M. Sc, M.S., M.B.A., PhD) 5. Internship Head (for all taught programs) The team under the Placement and Internship Governing Council can be broadly divided into: 1. Verticals: These are the intra-department teams which are three-tiered The department teams will be separate for both the UG and PG programs, with representation for all departments in the UG and PG teams. The internship process will be jointly run by the same team for all the taught programs. 7 Horizontals: These are the inter-department teams which are two-tiered These teams will handle all the things that aren’t under the purview of the department teams. Further details can be found in the Rulebook for Placement & Internship Cell. 8 2. Career Development Cell – Research (CDC-R) Team: The CDC-R is an umbrella team for conceptualizing, undertaking and implementing all activities focused towards the personal and professional development of the scholars of the Institute. It handles all activities aimed towards enriching, empowering and enhancing the information, opportunities and facilities available to a scholar on campus. This in turn helps them decide and advance in their desired career choice with the right set of tools and outlook. The set of activities which can be taken up by CDC-R includes, but not limited to: ● Placement Preparation ● Scholars Career Sessions ● Mentorship with Industries ● Entrepreneurship Workshops ● Skills Enhancement Workshops ● Scholars Website (scholars.iitm.ac.in) ● Any and all initiatives aimed at improving the career prospects of the scholars Head - CDC-R: The CDC-R Head directly reports to the Research Affairs Secretary, and is appointed through a written application and an interview process. The interview panel shall contain the outgoing CDC -R Head and Research Affairs Secretary, the incoming Research Affairs Secretary and approved by the Advisor (CDC- R) . In case the position is unfilled (no applicant or all applicants are rejected by the panel), the Research Affairs Secretary shall occupy this position by default. 9 CDC-R Core team: The CDC-R team shall have the following teams and the number of cores per team are presented next to them. Each of the cores shall have team members working with them for implementing their activities. All the selections are based on written application and interview, and done in consultation with Advisor (CDC-R). # Team Name # of Cores Description of the Team 1 Placement Prep 1 Conduct placement related sessions such as mock interviews, blue book preparation, alumni lecture etc. 10 2 Events & Workshops 2 Conduct awareness sessions such as JDP/JSP Opportunities, Patenting Sessions, Post Doc Awareness etc. Focus on workshops and skill building (both technical and soft skills) such as Academic Writing, Analytics, LaTeX and department specific skills. 3 Entrepreneurship & Mentoring 2 Encourage scholars to pursue entrepreneurship and make them aware about the available facilities and opportunities on campus. They will also find mentors for the scholars in the industry and alumni to help them understand their sector better before sitting for placements. Total # of Cores 5 CDC-R Coordinators: Each Core Member shall select coordinators, in consultation with the RAS and Head-CDC-R Team. The coordinators shall be allocated based on the team requirements. The selection process is through a written application and an interview. The interview panel shall contain the Head CDC -R Team and at- least two cores. 3. Research Scholars Day (RSD) Team: The Research Scholars Day (RSD) team shall be responsible for conducting the annual research festival of IIT Madras, Research Scholars Day . The RSD would be the flagship festival of the Institute to celebrate the spirit of Research on the Campus and provide opportunities for the scholars to showcase their talents and interact with the distinguished industry and academic personalities including the alumni as well. The RSD Team shall be constituted for conducting this festival and other Scholar interaction events, and the CDC-R team and all other teams shall assist them with all possible help they would be needed. A few verticals shall be specific to the RSD team and recruitment shall be done for them separately at the appropriate t ime. Each of the verticals would be headed by 1 or 2 Cores and they shall have coordinators assisting them in executing the activities. 11 Head - RSD: The RSD Head directly reports to the Research Affairs Secretary, and is appointed through a written application and an interview process. The interview panel shall contain the outgoing RSD Head and Research Affairs Secretary, the incoming Research Affairs Secretary and approved by the Dean of Academic Research. In case the position is u nfilled (no applicant or all applicants are rejected by the panel), the Research Affairs Secretary shall occupy this position by default. RSD Core Team: The Core Team Members are selected through a written application, followed by an interview. The interview panel shall consist of Research Affairs Secretary, Head-RSD and the outgoing head and core members. The RSD Team shall be divided into the following verticals, each headed by Core Members. Some of the teams shall consist of the existing CDC-R teams. The complete list of teams is given. Duties and Responsibilities: ● Events Team The Events Team shall be responsible for all events during and before RSD. The event team plays a vital role in planning, coordinating, and flawlessly executing a wide range of events. Their responsibilities encompass types of event such as cultural events, lecture series, competitions, and ensuring effective communication and collaboration with speakers. Event team shall consist of a maximum of one core and five coordinators. ● Career Fair and Alumni relation This team shall be responsible for reaching out to the alumni to involve them in the festival in various ways. The team shall work with the Events & Operations team, the Alumni Relations Cell(ARC) and other stakeholders to increase the engagement of the alumni during the festival. It shall have 1 core and 12 maximum of 5 coordinators. ● Sponsorship and Finance The sponsorship & aegis team proactively seeks out potential sponsors and establishes meaningful partnerships. They actively engage with companies and organizations, presenting compelling sponsorship opportunities and demonstrating the value and benefits of supporting RSD events. This team shall be responsible for procuring and managing RSD Merchandise. This team is also responsible for maintaining the finances for the festival. They shall help allocate budget and handle the online merchandise sales, event expenses, logistic costs , manage vendors and maintain a record. They shall handle the administration with any queries regarding finances and reimbursements for the expenses. This team shall have a maximum of two cores and six coordinators. ● Logistics & Support Team The Logistics & Support Team shall be responsible for the smooth conduct of RSD by making necessary arrangements such as venue selection, accommodation & transportation management, staff & volunteer management, equipment & supply management, Hospitality of Guests etc. This team shall have one core and five coordinators. ● Visual Communication Team This team shall be responsible for creation of multimedia content related to RSD like Logo, banner, brochure, website and social media design (creation and maintanance), and shall also be responsible for all decorations (ambience) at the venues of RSD. This team will have maximum of one core and 5 coordinators. ● Outreach and promotion Team This team shall be responsible for marketing, promotion, and media outreach across various platforms including Facebook, Instagram, and LinkedIn. They employ strategic tactics to create awareness about the various RSD events. This team is also expected to Gather feedback, analyse .the success of the event and create a report. This team shall comprise of maximum of one core and 5 coordinators. Selection Procedure The Core Members are selected through a written application and interview process. The panel of interviewers shall contain the RAS, Head and the Cores from the previous year. This panel recommends names for selection, and their selections are confirmed after taking approval from the Dean (Academic Research). The Coordinators shall be selected through a written application and interview process, with the panel 13 containing the Head, and the Core Members of the Team. Removal Procedure Underperforming cores shall be removed in consultati on with the Dean (Academic Research). Cores shall be also removed if they are found guilty by any disciplinary committee, as the RSD team demands the highest professional integrity and ethics. Coordinators shall be removed, if they underperform, but only after a thorough performance review by the cores and RAS on their performance in the team. They also shall be removed if they are found guilty by any disciplinary committee. Removal of any member from the team must be documented in the form of a report and shall be made available, on demand, to the Dean(AR) and/or SLC. The RAS shall maintain the reports for core members, and the respective cores for the coordinators. Official Online Presence of RSD: Facebook ID: https://www.facebook.com/rsdIITM/ Website: www.rsdiitmadras.com 4. Research Connect (R-Connect) Team: Research Connect is an initiative started in the year 2016 for improving Industry-Academia Interactions and Collaborations. A typical R-Connect Event is composed of a visit by industrial R&D to research labs at IIT Madras working in a similar area of research and interaction with students and faculty. It is aimed at bringing about potential research collaborations, job/internship opportunities, sponsored MS/PhD Programs etc. Head - RConnect: The RConnect Head directly reports to the Research Affairs Secretary, and is appointed through a written application and an interview process. The interview panel shall contain the outgoing RConnect Head and Research Affairs Secretary, the incoming Research Affairs Secretary and approved by the Advisor (RConnect) . In case the position is unfilled (no applicant or all applicant s are rejected by the panel), the Research Affairs Secretary shall occupy this position by default. 14 Duties and Responsibilities: The members of the team shall coordinate with other institute bodies/organizations like I&AR Office, Centre for IC&SR, Placement Team etc. to establish contact with industrial R&D Labs and co -ordinate their visit to the Institute Research Labs. The Team shall consist of a RConnect Head, a maximum of 5 Cores and 5 Coordinators each. # Team Name # of Cores Description of the Team 1 Alumni Connect 1 Helps to connect and organize meets with Alumni of IIT Madras, to know their experience and current work cultures of Industries. 2 Industry Connect 1 Helps to connect the R&D work going on the industries, with the research work happening in the IIT Madras labs. 3 Research Magazine 1 Helps to gather and publish record of all the research work, events, achievements done by the scholars in IIT Madras 4 Research Event Connect 1 Helps to organize research exhibitions that will feature industry peoples and scholars under common roof, to showcase their research work 5 Foreign Connect 1 Helps to establish connections between foreign industries and the research work happening in the IIT Madras labs. 15 Selection Procedure The Core Members are selected through a written application and interview process. The panel of interviewers shall contain the RAS, Head and the Head & Cores from the previous year. This panel recommends names for selection, and their selections are confirmed after taking approval from the Dean (Academic Research). The Coordinators shall be selected through a written application and interview process, with the panel containing the Head and the Core Members of the Team. Removal Procedure Underperforming cores shall be removed in consultation with the Dean (Academic Research). Cores shall be also removed if they are found guilty by any disciplinary committee, as the Research Connect team demands the highest professional integrity and ethics. Coordinators shall be removed, if they underperform, but only after a thorough performance review by the cores and RAS on their performance in the team. They also shall be removed if they are found guilty by any disciplinary committee. Removal of any member from the team must be documented in the form of a report and shall be made available, on demand, to the Dean(AR) and/or SLC. The RAS shall maintain the reports for core members, and the respective cores for the coordinators and super coordinators. Panel of Mentors Research Connect, requires a certain continuity across the years, as the goals are long-term in nature. Hence, a panel of mentors, consisting of interested previous cores/Research Affairs Secretaries, may be formed, to act in an advisory capacity to the team. This panel may have a tenure of six months from the date of formation. The panel should be approved by Dean (AR). 16 6. Problem-Solving Cell – Research: Under the RAS, the problem-solving cell is a body responsible for solving problems faced by scholars at an institute and residential level. With an idea to help scholars solve their issues, a new Problem-solving cell has been proposed by the RAS during the 2023 -2024 academic year. The motivation to help scholars has arrived from the recent unfortunate events happened inside the campus. The pr ime motive of this unit is to identify the common problems faced by scholars through surveys and arrive at the solutions to resolve the issues. The head of the problem -solving cell should directly report to the RAS. The problem -solving cell deals with all kinds of issues faced by scholars such as work -place harassment, academic/administration related issues, guide -student relationships, mental health etc. Scholars facing mental health issues can approach the head of the problem-solving cell. With the help of wellness centre and MiTr, Sathi the student will be given a proper counselling in order to prevent the scholar taking any sensitive actions. During the entire process, the identity of the scholar will be protected and anonymity is maintained. The structure of the problem-solving cell is created with 4 cores responsible in carrying out various activities with the help of the coordinators. The cores will have regular meetings with the head to discuss the progress and jointly come up with common ideas to resolve the scholar’s issues. Important decisions that can have a potential impact on the administrative activities should be discussed with the RAS and the RAS need to make a final decision preserving the common interests of the scholars Head - Problem-Solving Cell – Research: The Problem solving cell - Research Head directly reports to the Research Affairs Secretary, and is appointed through a written application and an interview process. The interview panel shall contain the outgoing past PSC-R Head and Research Affairs Secretary, the incoming Research Affairs Secretary and approved by the Advisor (PSC-R) . In case the position is unfilled (no applicant or all applicants are rejected by the panel), the Research Affairs Secretary shall occupy this position by default. 17 Duties and Responsibilities: The members of the team shall coordinate with other institute bodies/organizations like Wellness center, Mitr ,Sathi etc.The Team shall consist of a Problem-Solving Cell Head, a maximum of 4 Cores and 5 Coordinators each. • Personal Problems These vertical deals all kinds of activities that result in the harassment of scholars at the workplace. The activities could be sexual, mental pressure, character assassination, humiliation etc. that could potentially impact the mental h ealth of the scholars. Necessary action will be taken by the team members if a harassment at workplace is reported to concern authorities. This cell takes care of all issues related to hospitality, starting with the hostels for unmarried and scholars to th e quarters allocation to married scholars. This team shall comprise of maximum of one core and 5 coordinators • Professional problems All the issues faced by the scholars due to academic and administration will be taken care of. The academic issues include courses, grades etc. and administration issues such as financial, project fundings, research resources etc. will be handled. This team shall comprise of maximum of one core and 5 coordinators • Wellness With the help of wellness centre and MiTr, this cell helps scholars resolve the mental health related issues. We try to arrange necessary counselling sessions to the scholars, and make sure to maintain 18 anonymity and confidentiality in every case, and we will raise funds. This team shall comprise of maximum of one core and 5 coordinators • Wellness events and helping hands: This vertical primarily focusses on organizing the awareness programmes to enlighten the scholars about the importance of mental health, and also promises every scholar that they could reach us even with a minute issue bothering them. This team shall comprise of maximum of one core and 5 coordinators Selection Procedure The Core Members are selected through a written application and interview process. The panel of interviewers shall contain the RAS, Head and the Head & Cores from the previous year. This panel recommends names for selection, and their selections are confirmed after taking approval from the Dean (Academic Research). The coordinators shall be selected through a written application and interview process, with the panel containing the Head and the Core Members of the Team. Removal Procedure Underperforming cores shall be removed in consultation with the Dean (Academic Res earch). Cores shall be also removed if they are found guilty by any disciplinary committee, as the Research Connect team demands the highest professional integrity and ethics. Coordinators shall be removed, if they underperform, but only after a thorough performance review by the cores and RAS on their performance in the team. They also shall be removed if they are found guilty by any disciplinary committee. Removal of any member from the team must be documented in the form of a report and shall be made available, on demand, to the Dean(AR) and/or SLC. The RAS shall maintain the reports for core members, and the respective cores for the coordinators and super coordinators. 7. Research Clubs: We plan to form research clubs in every department to improve the connections between the scholars. Assigning a dedicated help desk personnel for each department With an aim to improve the research connectivity between the scholars, R-clubs has been proposed by the RAS during the 2023 -2024 academic year. This team has a potential to help the scholars from 19 various departments to connect with the scholars working in a similar domain. For instance, one scholar working on a commercial software can easily get in touch with another scholar who has experience in using the same commercial software, this way we can improve the research progress of every scholar at IITM which would potentially impact the institute’s research output. The head of R - clubs should directly report to the RAS. The R-clubs has 4 cores and each of them should have regular interactions with the head of R -clubs. The cores are responsible to perform all the ground -level tasks with the help of coordinators. The coordinators should coordinate with the department legislators to create a group con taining a representative from each and every lab in the department. The representative should be responsible to provide the details of every scholar, laboratory equipment under that particular scholar or the commercial/opensource software being used by the scholar for his/her research. The details should be handed over to the respective cores and the cores will be responsible to make the details available to all the scholars at IITM. The updates during the entire process should be communicated to the head a nd the RAS. The important decisions should be made jointly with a proper discussion with the team head and the RAS. Head – Research Clubs: The Research Clubs Head directly reports to the Research Affairs Secretary, and is appointed through a written application and an interview process. The interview panel shall contain the outgoing past R- Clubs Head and Research Affairs Secretary, the incoming Research Affairs Secretary and approved by the Advisor (R-Clubs) . In case the position is unfilled (no applicant or all applicants are rejected by the panel), the Research Affairs Secretary shall occupy this position by default. 20 Duties and Responsibilities: The members of the team shall coordinate with all the department’s scholars with the help of Department research legislators. The Team shall consist of a R-Clubs Head, a maximum of 4 Cores and 5 Coordinators each. Build school sessions: The core is responsible for identify and approach the scholars with various skill sets, and conduct skill-sharing sessions with the help of the scholars. Sessions related to innovations should be conducted in order to make the scholar brain-storm together and arrive at innovate ideas that would potentially become start-up ideas. Frequent sessions should be organized in order to communicate common research related issues such as the equipment/software: Inter-department connections: The two cores are responsible to develop the research connections among the laboratories in a department as well as the between each and every department. The cores should perform all the ground-level activities such as obtaining the details (equipment, software, Research Vlogs etc.) of every scholars with the help of coordinators, department legislators and the laboratory representatives. The data should be made available to all the scholars through brochures/websites. Research facilities: The core is responsible to make all the details of the research facilities at IITM available for the scholars. Details about the common research facilities such as the Sophisticated Analytical Instruments Facility (SAIF), Central Electronics Centre (CEC), High Performance Computing Environment (HPCE) should be made available for the scholars. The core is also responsible to answer the queries related to the research facilities available on campus. The information guide that helps understanding the working, procedure to use the equipment should be made available to the scholars. Selection Procedure The Core Members are selected through a written application and interview process. The panel of interviewers shall contain the RAS, Head and the Head & Cores from the previous year. This panel recommends names for selection, and their selections are confirmed after taking approval from the Dean (Academic Research). The Coordinators shall be selected through a written application and interview process, with the panel containing the Head and the Core Members of the Team. Removal Procedure Underperforming cores shall be removed in consultation with the Dean (Academic Research). Cores shall be also removed if they are found guilty by any disciplinary committee, as the Research Connect team demands the highest professional integrity and ethics. 21 Coordinators shall be removed, if they underperform, but only after a thorough performance re view by the cores and RAS on their performance in the team. They also shall be removed if they are found guilty by any disciplinary committee. Removal of any member from the team must be documented in the form of a report and shall be made available, on d emand, to the Dean(AR) and/or SLC. The RAS shall maintain the reports for core members, and the respective cores for the coordinators and super coordinators. Research Affairs Council (RAC) Due to the removal of the Councilor position from the Constitution in 2020, RAC is suspended. The RAS Executive Team and Research Legislators shall carry on the work of RAC in spirit. Resignation Procedure Resignation of the Research Affairs Secretary: Any member of the Executive Council who wishes to resign his/her Position of Responsibility may do so by writing a resignation letter to the Speaker and the Chairman, Board of Students, detailing reasons behind the same along with the password to their officia l email -id. The Research Affairs Secretary shall have resigned upon official communication of the same to the Student Legislative Council by the Speaker. Post-resignation Procedure: In case a member of the Executive Council resigns with more than three months available for the scheduled General Elections, the Student Election Commission shall conduct an election for that particular Position of Responsibility immediately, with the student so elected continuing to hold office till the end of the academic year. In other cases, the Dean (Students) shall give additional charge of the vacated Position of Responsibility to a member of the Executive Council. Statement of Expenditure The Executive Council and Student Government Organizations shall present a financial statement detailing the expenditure of the approved budget at least once a semester to the Student Legislative Council in addition to a report about their financial statement to the corresponding Standing Committee once in two months. files.67c2bdbb71: Students’ General Secretary Rulebook Roles and responsibilities 2 SGS Executive Committee 3-4 Extra Mural Lectures 5-6 Saathi 7-8 Disaster Management Committee 9-10 IIT for Villages 10 Institute Web Operations 11-12 Pragati 13-17 Campus Facilities Monitoring Facilities 18-19 2 Roles and Responsibilities The Students' General Secretary shall: • Coordinate the work of the other Executive Council members; • Represent the views of the General Student Body to the Senate; • Handle matters and monitor organizations, committees or clubs which do not fall under the purview of other Executive Council members; • Represent the students in all tendering processes for student facilities inside the Institute; • Be an ex-officio member of any committee which may be set up by the Administration for matters related to the general amenities provided to the students; • Be one of the student members of the hospital, transport, canteen, security and other such committees which may be formed for providing amenities to the students; • Be a member of the Hostel Disciplinary Committee (HDC), the Committee for Monitoring of General Facilities for Students (CMGFS), the Mess Monitoring and Control Committee (MMCC) • Be an ex-officio member of any committee/team/organization to represent students in matters related to disciplinary action. Student Bodies fall under the Students’ General Secretary 3 SGS EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE SGS Executive Committee monitors the issues affecting the students. It resolves them as the earliest, devises initiatives to improve the student community's lives, and coordinates and assists various SGS Bodies in their functioning. Initiatives: Before taking any steps forward in implementing any initiatives, the initiative mission-vision statement explaining the goals of the initiatives should be sent to the SGS for consultation and approval. Structure: The Team Structure is: • Core(only 1) • Member Core Selection: Core Selection is initiated and processed by a Panel containing the Students’ General Secretary, former Students’ General Secretary, and former SGS Executive Committee Core. The application procedure will be intimated to the student community in a call for applications and they should have CGPA greater than or equal to 6.5. Member: Selection is done by the Core and Students’ General Secretary through a process intimated to the student community in a call for application forms 4 Answerability: • All the members are answerable to the Core of SGS Executive Committee. • In turn, SGS Executive Committee Core is answerable to SGS. • SGS will represent SGS Executive Committee and will be answerable to SLC if required. • One can be disqualified from the team only upon consulting with the SGS and submitting a request for disqualification along with a report. 5 Extra Mural Lectures EML is the Institute’s official forum for hosting lectures.
